findings.message: Preserve the assign utility exposed to plugins. Removing this export also removes `md.utils.assign`, which existing plugins still call. In particular, the declared `markdown-it-container` 4.x dependency uses it during initialization, and `support/demo_template/index.mjs` installs that plugin, so the demo now fails with `TypeError: md.utils.assign is not a function`. Keep a compatibility export, even if internal callers switch to `Object.assign`.

This removes `assign`, `isString` and `has` from the utils exports. Those exports are public API: `MarkdownIt#utils` exposes the whole module to plugins (src/markdownit.ts:322-330). Many third-party plugins call `md.utils.assign`, `md.utils.isString` or `md.utils.has`, and with this change they will throw `TypeError: ... is not a function` at runtime. That is a breaking change and needs a major version bump plus a migration note. Otherwise, keep the helpers as deprecated aliases, e.g. `assign = Object.assign`.

`utils.assign` threw a TypeError when the source was not an object. `Object.assign` silently copies index keys from a string: `md.set('foo')` now writes keys '0', '1', '2' into options instead of failing. Bad input to `set()` is no longer caught.

`utils.isString` also matched boxed String objects (`new String('commonmark')`), but `typeof` does not. A boxed preset name passed to the constructor or to `configure()` (line 383) is now treated as an options object instead of a preset name. This is a small edge case, but the behavior change is not mentioned anywhere.
